question: A 34-year-old woman presents with recurrent panic attacks that have been worsening over the past 5 weeks. She also says she has been seeing things that are not present in reality and is significantly bothered by a short attention span which has badly affected her job in the past 6 months. No significant past medical history. No current medications. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Her BMI is 34 kg/m2. Physical examination is unremarkable. The patient has prescribed antipsychotic medication. She expresses concerns about any effects of the new medication on her weight. Which of the following medications would be the best course of treatment in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Recurrent panic attacks" -> "Seeing things not present in reality" -> "Short attention span affecting job" -> "Symptoms suggestive of psychosis" -> "Prescribed antipsychotic medication" -> "Concerns about medication effects on weight" -> 70%

CHAIN: "BMI of 34 kg/m2" -> "Increased risk of metabolic side effects with certain antipsychotic medications" -> "Consideration for weight-neutral or weight-friendly antipsychotic" -> "Avoiding medications known for significant weight gain" -> "Choosing Ziprasidone or Aripiprazole over Olanzapine or Clozapine" -> 80%
analysis: Given the patient's symptoms of recurrent panic attacks, visual hallucinations, short attention span, and obesity (BMI 34 kg/m2), the best course of treatment would be to prescribe an antipsychotic medication that is less likely to cause weight gain. Among the options provided, Ziprasidone is known to have a lower risk of weight gain compared to Olanzapine and Clozapine.
